what: Simpson Manufacturing makes the metal connectors that hold wooden buildings together: joist hangers, hurricane ties, anchors and the screws and fasteners that go with them.
customers: Builders, framers and contractors, through lumber yards and building supply dealers.
money: wood and concrete construction connectors and fasteners
the same products in European markets
moat: Connectors specified by engineers and written into building codes, tested and approved for specific loads, which means a substitute must repeat that testing to be allowed.
risks: Housing starts drive demand and they have been weak
Steel prices move the cost base
opportunities: A 14.8% net margin and $496M of free cash flow on $2.4B of revenue, exceptional for a hardware maker
Code changes keep requiring more connectors per house, especially in hurricane and earthquake regions
watch: North American volume growth and the operating margin.
